title.narrative: Olive and Wheat Value Chains Recovery in Syria – GranOlio Syria
Recupero delle filiere del frumento e dell’olivo in Siria – GranOlio Syria

description.narrative: L’iniziativa in oggetto mira a contribuire alla sicurezza alimentare e al rilancio sostenibile del settore agricolo siriano attraverso il rafforzamento delle filiere del frumento e dell’olivo. In questa cornice, la strategia operativa è articolata in tre componenti tra loro interconnesse. La prima riguarda il rafforzamento istituzionale e tecnico-scientifico e punta a potenziare le capacità del MAAR e degli enti collegati nella ricerca, produzione e certificazione di sementi e olio d’oliva di qualità, mediante formazione su miglioramento genetico, controllo qualità e analisi di semi e olio, riabilitazione dei laboratori di GCSAR, GOSM e Olive Bureau, sviluppo di linee guida e protocolli per certificazione e tracciabilità e scambi tecnici con istituzioni italiane. La seconda componente sostiene la riattivazione produttiva e gli agricoltori, con l’obiettivo di incrementare produttività e qualità delle colture e favorire la ripresa economica rurale; prevede la distribuzione di sementi certificate, piantine e piccoli macchinari secondo il modello cost recovery, l’introduzione di buone pratiche agronomiche e sistemi irrigui efficienti, prove dimostrative su varietà resilienti, assistenza tecnica continua e supporto alla creazione di microimprese femminili e giovanili lungo la catena del valore. La terza componente è dedicata a sensibilizzazione, visibilità e governance, migliorando conoscenza, coordinamento e comunicazione dei risultati tramite workshop, campagne di divulgazione, materiali dedicati alla Cooperazione italiana, funzionamento dello Steering Committee e della Segreteria Tecnica e attuazione del sistema RBM di monitoraggio e valutazione. Le tre componenti avanzano in modo sinergico lungo un percorso che va dalla definizione di baseline e piani operativi all’espansione delle buone pratiche, fino alla capitalizzazione e alla sostenibilità.

The initiative aims to contribute to food security and to the sustainable recovery of the Syrian agricultural sector by strengthening the wheat and olive value chains. Within this framework, the operational strategy is structured into three interconnected components. The first focuses on institutional and technical-scientific strengthening, aiming to enhance the capacities of the MAAR and related institutions in the research, production and certification of quality seeds and olive oil through training on genetic improvement, quality control and seed and oil analysis, the rehabilitation and equipment of GCSAR, GOSM and Olive Bureau laboratories, the development of guidelines and protocols for certification and traceability, and technical exchanges with Italian institutions. The second component supports productive reactivation and farmers, with the objective of increasing the productivity and quality of wheat and olive crops and fostering the economic recovery of rural communities; it includes the distribution of certified seeds, seedlings and small machinery through a cost-recovery model, the introduction of good agronomic practices and efficient irrigation systems, demonstration activities on more resilient varieties, continuous technical assistance throughout the crop cycle, and support for the creation of women’s and youth-led microenterprises along the value chain. The third component focuses on awareness, visibility and governance, improving knowledge, coordinated management and communication of results through workshops, scientific outreach campaigns, communication materials dedicated to the Italian Cooperation, the functioning of the Steering Committee and Technical Secretariat, and the implementation of the RBM monitoring and evaluation system. The three components advance synergistically along a pathway that moves from baseline data collection and operational planning to the expansion of good practices, culminating in capitalization and long-term sustainability.

By 2030, achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value

By 2030, double the agricultural productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers, in particular women, indigenous peoples, family farmers, pastoralists and fishers, including through secure and equal access to land, other productive resources and inputs, knowledge, financial services, markets and opportunities for value addition and non-farm employment
By 2030, ensure equal access for all women and men to affordable and quality technical, vocational and tertiary education, including university

Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all

Promote development-oriented policies that support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation, and encourage the formalization and growth of micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises, including through access to financial services
Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all
